nodes.label: mergeLeadFields — pure merge function
nodes.rationale: Pure, database-free, exercised by merge.test.ts. Rules: never null out a known value (an incoming null or absent field is ignored); a known value is never overwritten by a different one for name/phone/email/notes; timestamps only advance, never move backwards; terminal statuses never regress to an earlier status; estimated_value only rises, never falls. Returns {} when there is nothing to change.

nodes.label: test:prove-isolation / prove-isolation.sh
nodes.rationale: Loosens leads_tenant_isolation to using (true), asserts the suite goes red, then restores it. Always run it after touching policies or grants: a green isolation test that cannot detect a breach is false confidence.

nodes.label: recordLeadEvent()
nodes.rationale: No-ops when a duplicate dedupe_key arrives, making retried deliveries idempotent.

nodes.label: upsertLead()
nodes.rationale: Matches on any normalized identity and merges onto the existing lead instead of inserting a second one.

nodes.label: withIngestScope(db, customerId, fn)
nodes.rationale: Sets a transaction-local app.customer_id and switches to ingest_role. Needs a real transaction, so a stateless HTTP driver will not work.

nodes.label: drizzle-kit generate --custom
nodes.rationale: Use --custom for raw SQL (roles, grants) rather than hand-writing a file, because it registers the journal entry that migrate reads.

nodes.label: customers table
nodes.rationale: The tenant; 1:1 with an auth.users row today.

nodes.label: Migrations run against DATABASE_URL_DIRECT
nodes.rationale: DDL needs session state a transaction pooler will not hold.

nodes.label: detection_settings table
nodes.rationale: Per-tenant thresholds feeding detectLeaks; defaults mirror the existing module constants exactly so behaviour is unchanged until a customer edits them.

nodes.label: ingest_role (NOBYPASSRLS)
nodes.rationale: Ingest is unauthenticated — a form tool POSTs to a secret URL, so there is no auth.uid() and the authenticated policies cannot apply. ingest_role is NOBYPASSRLS so a bug cannot write across tenants, and an unset scope fails closed.

nodes.label: lead_events table
nodes.rationale: Ingest audit trail plus idempotency key: unique(customer_id, dedupe_key). Also holds raw_payload and the per-ingest parse_errors/parse_warnings, which are diagnostics of a delivery rather than attributes of a lead.

nodes.label: lead_identities table
nodes.rationale: Contact points a lead is reachable at — the merge key. unique(customer_id, kind, value_normalized) is what lets the same human arriving through two channels collapse onto one lead.

nodes.label: lead_sources table
nodes.rationale: A webhook URL, forwarding address, or CSV upload. Carries webhook_token plus webhook_token_previous for rotation overlap, and a unique inbound_address.

nodes.label: leads table
nodes.rationale: The lead itself: surrogate uuid PK, email/phone plus their normalized forms, lead_status enum, estimated_value in integer cents, indexed on (customer_id, created_at desc) and (customer_id, status).

nodes.label: push_tokens table
nodes.rationale: Devices to notify, empty until the notification phase — created now so that phase needs no tenancy migration. last_seen_at tracks token rot.

nodes.label: public.current_customer_id() helper function
nodes.rationale: security definer, stable, search_path = public; selects customers.id where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) so the customer lookup is written once instead of per policy.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL_DIRECT vs pooled DATABASE_URL
nodes.rationale: Functions use the Supavisor transaction pooler; drizzle-kit migrations use the direct/session connection because poolers in transaction mode reject the session state DDL needs. SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is server-only and never client-exposed; VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ anon keys are public by design.

nodes.label: DetectionConfig — parameterized leak thresholds
nodes.rationale: detectLeaks gains a third positional arg defaulting to DEFAULT_DETECTION_CONFIG { slowReplyHours: 24, staleQuoteDays: 7 }, so both existing call sites and every test keep working untouched — and detection_settings has something to bind to.

nodes.label: ESM / "type": "module" packaging trap
nodes.rationale: packages/core emits ESM but its exports.require points at the same ESM file, so a Vercel Node function doing require('@missed-lead/core') fails. Add "type":"module" to core and db and drop the false require conditions. Separately, vite aliases @missed-lead/core to dist, so the root build must compile workspaces first or core edits stay invisible.

nodes.label: supabase.auth.getClaims() for JWT verification
nodes.rationale: Preferred over getUser(): getClaims verifies the JWT against the cached JWKS endpoint /.well-known/jwks.json instead of always round-tripping to the Auth server, removing one network hop per request. jose + cached JWKS is the manual equivalent.

nodes.label: Greedy SPA rewrite in vercel.json
nodes.rationale: {"source":"/(.*)"} is maximally greedy; Vercel normally matches api/ functions before rewrites but that precedence is not worth relying on. Change to the negative lookahead /((?!api/).*) and verify with a real request.

nodes.label: ingest_role scoped by transaction-local app.customer_id
nodes.rationale: A dedicated role that is deliberately NOT BYPASSRLS. Each ingest write runs in a transaction that does `set local app.customer_id = '<resolved-from-webhook-token>'`, with policies keyed on current_setting('app.customer_id', true)::uuid for both using and with check. A bug in the ingest handler then cannot write across tenants — the DB refuses. Requires a transaction-capable connection (Supavisor transaction mode + postgres.js), not a stateless HTTP driver — a second reason Supabase beat Neon.

nodes.label: Cross-tenant isolation test (phase acceptance gate)
nodes.rationale: vitest at packages/db/src/__tests__/tenant-isolation.test.ts against a local Supabase. Seeds customer A (3 leads) and B (2 leads) from real supabase.auth.signUp() sessions and asserts: correct row counts per tenant, B's lead id returns 0 rows (empty not error), insert with the other tenant's customer_id is rejected by with check, cross-tenant update affects 0 rows, repeated for lead_events, lead_identities, detection_settings, push_tokens, and that the ingest path with A's webhook token cannot write B's customer_id.

nodes.label: LEAD_STATUSES as single source of truth
nodes.norm_label: lead_statuses as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: The status list was hardcoded in four places and had already diverged (revenue.ts:23 counts booked as recovered while leaks.ts:21 treats it as merely terminal). Export LEAD_STATUSES / TERMINAL_STATUSES / RECOVERED_STATUSES and generate pgEnum('lead_status', LEAD_STATUSES) rather than retyping it. Keep the booked-is-recovered behaviour — a product question, not a Phase 1 refactor — but make it named instead of accidental.

nodes.label: Email/phone normalization rules
nodes.rationale: Pure and unit-tested in packages/core. email → trim().toLowerCase() and nothing cleverer: no gmail dot-stripping or plus-tag removal, because that over-merges distinct people and is unrecoverable once merged. phone → strip non-digits, drop a leading 1 if 11 digits, keep the last 10 (NANP-shaped, fits the local-service-business target); the original stays untouched in phone.

nodes.label: packages/db (@missed-lead/db) workspace package
nodes.rationale: Schema, migrations, and repository functions kept out of packages/core so core stays a pure, dependency-free engine.

nodes.label: Parser date-field bug (last_contact_at / next_follow_up_at)
nodes.rationale: Both fields are in HEADER_MAP but never written into the pushed object, so every CSV lead looks no_reply and slow_reply / no_follow_up / stale_quote are unreachable — half the engine is dead, and the DB would faithfully persist nulls the parser can never fill. Fixed TDD: failing test in parser.test.ts first.

nodes.label: resolveCustomer — session → customer_id resolver
nodes.rationale: api/_lib/auth.ts returns Resolved { ok: true, userId, customerId, jwt } or AuthFailure { ok: false, status: 401|403, code }. Failure modes explicit, never silent: missing/malformed header → 401; valid JWT but no customers row → 403 no_customer, never an auto-create, because silently minting tenants on a stray token is how cross-tenant bugs start.

nodes.label: tenant_isolation policy shape
nodes.rationale: Repeated per tenant table: for all to authenticated, using and with check both customer_id = (select public.current_customer_id()). RLS is enabled in the same migration that creates the table, plus force row level security so even the table owner is subject to policy.

nodes.label: authUid — prebuilt SQL fragment
nodes.rationale: authUid is a prebuilt SQL fragment, but whether it already renders the (select auth.uid()) performance wrapping is still unverified; if not, use sql`(select auth.uid())` directly.

nodes.label: authUsers — typed auth.users table
nodes.rationale: A real win: customers.auth_user_id can reference authUsers.id as a typed Drizzle FK with onDelete: 'cascade' instead of hand-written SQL against auth.users. Columns include id uuid PK, email, phone, emailConfirmedAt, phoneConfirmedAt, lastSignInAt, createdAt, updatedAt.

nodes.label: drizzle-orm/supabase exports
nodes.rationale: From drizzle-orm/supabase/rls.d.ts: anonRole, authenticatedRole, serviceRole, postgresRole, supabaseAuthAdminRole (all PgRole), authUid (SQL<unknown>), authUsers (PgTable), plus unused realtimeMessages/realtimeTopic. Everything needed is present.

nodes.label: .enableRLS()
nodes.rationale: Confirmed at drizzle-orm/pg-core/table.d.ts:22 as `enableRLS: () => Omit<PgTableWithColumns<T>, 'enableRLS'>`, chained off pgTable(...). Defining any pgPolicy already enables RLS implicitly, so .enableRLS() is for tables that need RLS with NO policies — exactly right for tables only the service role should touch.

nodes.label: drizzle.config entities.roles.provider = 'supabase'
nodes.rationale: Confirmed from drizzle-kit/index.d.mts:131-137 as entities?: { roles?: boolean | { provider?: 'supabase'|'neon'|(string&{}); exclude?: string[]; include?: string[] } }. Setting provider: 'supabase' makes drizzle-kit treat Supabase's built-in roles as pre-existing so it does not emit DROP ROLE for them. Goes in the config from the first migration.

nodes.label: pgRole('ingest_role') declaration
nodes.rationale: Tenant policies use to: authenticatedRole; the custom ingest_role needs pgRole('ingest_role') declared, or a raw SQL migration if role creation needs attributes drizzle-kit cannot express.

nodes.label: PgPolicyToOption accepts a PgRole object
nodes.rationale: 'public' | 'current_role' | 'current_user' | 'session_user' | (string & {}) | PgPolicyToOption[] | PgRole — so imported role constants can be passed to `to` directly without stringifying.

nodes.label: pgPolicy(name, config)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed from drizzle-orm/pg-core/policies.d.ts: PgPolicyConfig is { as?: 'permissive'|'restrictive'; for?: 'all'|'select'|'insert'|'update'|'delete'; to?: PgPolicyToOption; using?: SQL; withCheck?: SQL }. Policies are hand-written with pgPolicy; if one cannot be expressed, a raw SQL migration is acceptable and better than fighting the abstraction.

nodes.label: Verified: Drizzle + Supabase RLS API surface
nodes.norm_label: verified: drizzle + supabase rls api surface
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-08-24 against the installed packages, not docs or memory, because the schema work was blocked on an unverified API surface.

nodes.label: Isolation assertions go through an anon-key client carrying a user JWT
nodes.norm_label: isolation assertions go through an anon-key client carrying a user jwt
nodes.rationale: A service-role client bypasses RLS and would make the suite pass while proving nothing.

nodes.label: RLS grants nothing
nodes.rationale: Policies filter WITHIN privileges a role already holds. Drizzle emits CREATE POLICY but never GRANT, so a new table without an explicit grant makes every query return error 42501. If you add a table, add its grants in the same migration.

nodes.label: Two dedupe mechanisms, for two different problems
nodes.norm_label: two dedupe mechanisms, for two different problems
nodes.rationale: Retried delivery → lead_events.dedupe_key → recordLeadEvent() no-ops. Same person via two channels → lead_identities → upsertLead() merges onto the existing lead. The second is the guard against double-counted revenue: if it breaks the product reports a wrong number rather than an obvious error, so its tests are worth keeping strict.

nodes.label: Use the anon key, never service_role, for isolation assertions
nodes.norm_label: use the anon key, never service_role, for isolation assertions
nodes.rationale: Two real sessions via supabase.auth.signUp(), then createClient(url, ANON_KEY, { global: { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + jwt }}}) per tenant. A service-role client bypasses RLS and would make the test pass while proving nothing — noted in a comment because it is the easiest way for this test to silently rot.

nodes.label: auth_user_id as a separate column from customers.id
nodes.norm_label: auth_user_id as a separate column from customers.id
nodes.rationale: Solo-owner today (team roles are an anti-feature), but keeping auth_user_id separate stops many-users-per-customer from requiring a migration of every FK later. Cheap insurance.

nodes.label: Split contact into email + phone in the DB
nodes.norm_label: split contact into email + phone in the db
nodes.rationale: Lead.contact is a single polymorphic, unvalidated string (email OR phone). You cannot reliably dedupe on that, and dedupe is load-bearing: PITFALLS #11's double-counted revenue is a correctness bug in the product's headline number. The TS Lead type keeps contact unchanged (all baseLead factories depend on it); the hydrator sets contact = email ?? phone — a mapping layer, not a breaking change.

nodes.label: estimated_value stored as integer cents
nodes.rationale: Integer cents throughout — a float column here silently corrupts money. The surrogate uuid id also replaces the positional `row-${i}` lead_id fallback, which collides across two imports of different files.

nodes.label: Identities get their own table
nodes.rationale: A lead can be reachable by both an email and a phone, and the same human can arrive twice through different pipes. A one-column dedupe key cannot model that. lead_identities lets an incoming lead match on ANY identity and merge onto the existing row.

nodes.label: Negative control — a green test that cannot fail is worse than no test
nodes.norm_label: negative control — a green test that cannot fail is worse than no test
nodes.rationale: Step 7's second half matters as much as the first: flipping one policy to using (true) must make the isolation suite FAIL. Confirm RED, then revert. A green isolation test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

nodes.label: pglite is not a substitute for Docker Supabase
nodes.norm_label: pglite is not a substitute for docker supabase
nodes.rationale: pglite has no GoTrue/auth schema, so auth.uid() does not exist and the policies under test cannot even be created. Docker is required. Flagged as unverified.

nodes.label: (select ...) InitPlan wrapping in policies
nodes.rationale: Wrapping in (select ...) lets Postgres cache the value as an InitPlan instead of re-evaluating it per row. Flagged for verification against the Supabase RLS performance best-practices page.

nodes.label: service_role fallback for ingest (rejected alternative)
nodes.rationale: Only if the pooler fights the GUC: service_role bypasses RLS entirely, reachable through a single auditable repository module (packages/db/src/repo/ingest.ts) taking customerId as every function's first argument. Tradeoff stated plainly — it moves isolation from the DB back into app code for the ingest path. The service-role key must never reach the client: server-only, unprefixed.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres over Neon
nodes.rationale: RLS policies need auth.uid(); with Supabase, Auth and Postgres are one vendor so policies read the verified JWT natively with zero cross-vendor plumbing and isolation genuinely lives in the DB. Neon's stateless HTTP driver also cannot hold the per-session/per-transaction variable RLS leans on, which would push isolation back up into app code — exactly what PITFALLS #8 warns against.

nodes.label: Two dedupe keys, precisely
nodes.rationale: Two different problems need two different keys. Duplicate POST (Typeform retry, Calendly redelivery) → dedupe_key = sha256(source_id + (provider_event_id ?? canonical_json(payload))) under unique(customer_id, dedupe_key) on lead_events. Same human via form AND email → normalized identity under unique(customer_id, kind, value_normalized) on lead_identities. One key cannot do both: idempotency is per-delivery, identity is per-person. Ingest resolves normalize → look up lead_identities → hit merges, miss inserts lead + identity. Upsert, never blind insert (PITFALLS #2).

nodes.label: The webhook isolation hole
nodes.rationale: Webhook ingest is unauthenticated by design — a form tool POSTs to a secret URL, so there is no user JWT, auth.uid() is null, and every authenticated-role policy evaluates false. This is the single biggest isolation risk in the whole design.

nodes.label: crudPolicy is Neon-only
nodes.rationale: crudPolicy exists only under drizzle-orm/neon/rls; there is no Supabase equivalent. This was an open question in the plan and the answer is 'not available', so every policy is written explicitly with pgPolicy — no shortcut.

nodes.label: Pinned versions drizzle-orm@0.45.2 / drizzle-kit@0.31.10
nodes.rationale: Do not use 1.0.0-beta.x. A v1 beta exists and the docs site banners it, but 0.45.2 is stable and its RLS surface is the one confirmed here. The 0.x→1.0 boundary is exactly where the RLS surface is most likely to have moved, so pin exactly.

nodes.label: Existing Stateless Monorepo (packages/core + packages/ui, Vite PWA, Expo 57)
nodes.norm_label: existing stateless monorepo (packages/core + packages/ui, vite pwa, expo 57)
nodes.rationale: Monorepo with core engine and Tamagui UI kit, Vite PWA on Vercel, Expo 57 mobile; stateless with no backend or DB today, which is why every new component is additive.

nodes.label: Onboarding UI (connection cards with live listening test)
nodes.norm_label: onboarding ui (connection cards with live listening test)
nodes.rationale: Live 'we're listening' test state proves the connection works without the owner needing technical help.

nodes.rationale: Existing product is stateless (no backend, no DB); v2 adds a backend tier so lead capture can happen continuously instead of via manual CSV upload.

nodes.label: Actionable Missed-Revenue Notification
nodes.rationale: Must contain a money figure, who and what they asked about, a channel badge, an age, and one tap-action. Notifications without a number get ignored; notifications without an owner action train users to swipe them away.

nodes.rationale: Deferred: Very high complexity; seeded via the drafted-reply hook but not part of v2.

nodes.label: CSV Upload as Optional 'Backfill Your History' Step
nodes.norm_label: csv upload as optional 'backfill your history' step
nodes.rationale: Demoted to optional and last so it never blocks the day-zero value moment.

nodes.label: Lead Detail with Drafted Reply (v2 hook)
nodes.norm_label: lead detail with drafted reply (v2 hook)

nodes.norm_label: form-capture tools' setup moment (zapier parser, calendly webhooks)

nodes.norm_label: missed-call text-back tools (proof of the core loop)

nodes.norm_label: onboarding flow for a non-technical salon owner

nodes.rationale: Deferred: High complexity, no user asks for it, and cron suffices.

nodes.rationale: Deferred: Med complexity but this is a solo-owner product today.

nodes.label: Project Research Summary
nodes.rationale: Synthesized inline on 2026-08-23 because researcher subagents were unavailable; consolidates STACK, FEATURES, ARCHITECTURE and PITFALLS.

nodes.label: Instant Awareness + One-Tap Response
nodes.rationale: The validated core loop owners pay for; it is the reason notification quality is treated as a table stake rather than polish.

nodes.label: Dedupe by Hash of Name + Contact
nodes.norm_label: dedupe by hash of name + contact
nodes.rationale: Ingest-time dedupe key prevents the same person counting twice when they arrive through more than one pipe.

nodes.label: Pitfall 7: Connection Pool Exhaustion
nodes.rationale: Every serverless invocation opens a Postgres connection and ~50 concurrent hits kill the DB. Warning sign: intermittent 'too many connections' at low traffic. Prevention: Neon HTTP serverless driver from day one, not node-postgres pooling. Phase 1 — a foundation decision that is expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: Prevention: Dedupe Key on Normalized Phone/Email + Fuzzy Name
nodes.norm_label: prevention: dedupe key on normalized phone/email + fuzzy name
nodes.rationale: Merges multiple sources onto one lead record; must exist in the schema from day one because retrofitting it corrupts historical revenue figures.

nodes.label: Pitfall 11: Double-Counted Lost Revenue
nodes.rationale: Same lead arrives via form AND forwarded email. Prevention: dedupe key on normalized phone/email plus fuzzy name, merging sources onto one lead record. Sits on the Phase 2/3 boundary, so the key must be designed into the schema in Phase 1 with enforcement from Phase 2 onward.

nodes.label: Pitfall 2: Duplicate POSTs
nodes.rationale: Typeform retries on timeout and Calendly redelivers. Prevention: idempotency key = hash of payload identity fields, upsert never blind insert, respond 200 in under 200ms and process async if slow. Phase 2.

nodes.label: Prevention: Idempotency Key = Hash of Payload Identity Fields
nodes.norm_label: prevention: idempotency key = hash of payload identity fields
nodes.rationale: Upsert rather than blind insert, and respond 200 within 200ms so senders do not retry in the first place.

nodes.label: Prevention: Neon HTTP Serverless Driver from Day One
nodes.norm_label: prevention: neon http serverless driver from day one
nodes.rationale: Adopted at foundation time specifically because swapping the data-access layer later is expensive.

nodes.label: Pitfall 8: RLS Forgotten and Tenant Data Leaks Across Accounts
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 8: rls forgotten and tenant data leaks across accounts
nodes.rationale: Prevention: enable RLS on ALL tables at migration time and add an integration test proving customer A cannot read customer B's leads. Phase 1.

nodes.label: Prevention: Accept Old and New Secret During Overlap Window
nodes.norm_label: prevention: accept old and new secret during overlap window
nodes.rationale: Rotation becomes non-breaking, and traffic to a dead token raises an alert instead of vanishing.

nodes.label: Serverless + Database Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering pool exhaustion and forgotten RLS; both are foundation-phase decisions that are expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: Pitfall 3: Secret Rotation Breaks Customer's Form Silently
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 3: secret rotation breaks customer's form silently
nodes.rationale: Warning sign: incoming requests to a dead token. Prevention: accept old and new secret during an overlap window and alert on hits to dead tokens. Phase 2.

nodes.label: Prevention: Prune Tokens on Expired/Invalid + Last-Seen Tracking
nodes.norm_label: prevention: prune tokens on expired/invalid + last-seen tracking
nodes.rationale: Turns silent send failures into observable token lifecycle state.

nodes.label: Pitfall 1: Unauthenticated Spam to Hook URLs
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 1: unauthenticated spam to hook urls
nodes.rationale: Bots scan /hook/* paths. Warning sign: junk leads appearing. Prevention: high-entropy secret in the URL path, reject unknown tokens silently, rate-limit per IP. Phase 2 (ingest).

nodes.label: Webhook Ingestion Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering spam to hook URLs, duplicate POSTs and silent secret-rotation breakage; all land in the ingest phase.

nodes.label: MongoDB (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: relational lead/event data wants SQL.

nodes.label: Postgres via Neon with @neondatabase/serverless driver (database recommendation)
nodes.norm_label: postgres via neon with @neondatabase/serverless driver (database recommendation)
nodes.rationale: HTTP-based driver avoids connection-pool exhaustion from serverless invocations; free tier fits the validation stage.

nodes.label: Prisma + pg Pool on Serverless (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected as the connection-pool exhaustion trap: each invocation opens a connection.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Foundation (DB + auth + RLS + schema with dedupe keys)
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: foundation (db + auth + rls + schema with dedupe keys)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 because it unblocks everything else; pitfalls named for this phase become its success criteria.

nodes.rationale: Sequenced second because it is the first user-visible value.

nodes.label: Watch Out For Checklist
nodes.rationale: Six highest-priority risks distilled from PITFALLS: Neon HTTP driver day one, RLS at migration plus cross-tenant test, idempotency/dedupe keys in the schema before first ingest, mail loops, cold permission asks, and PII retention before launch.

nodes.label: Detection Service (pure function in packages/core)

nodes.rationale: Detection output is a persisted record carrying a revenue estimate, which is what makes notifications and the dashboard actionable.

nodes.label: Nightly Cron Sweep
nodes.rationale: Catches leads that aged past the response threshold, which event-driven detection alone cannot observe.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Continuous Detection + Nightly Re-Sweep
nodes.norm_label: table stake: continuous detection + nightly re-sweep
nodes.rationale: Med complexity; depends on DB and cron.

nodes.label: Differentiators

nodes.label: Existing Leak-Detection + Revenue-Estimation Engine
nodes.rationale: All features feed it through the normalized Lead schema, so no engine rewrite is required.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Inbound Email Address per Customer
nodes.norm_label: table stake: inbound email address per customer
nodes.rationale: Med complexity; depends on the email worker.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Lead Normalization into Existing Schema
nodes.norm_label: table stake: lead normalization into existing schema
nodes.rationale: Low complexity; depends on the core engine and avoids any engine rewrite.

nodes.label: Differentiator: Live 'Revenue at Risk' Dashboard Counter

nodes.rationale: Med complexity; depends on all table stakes being in place.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Response-Time Threshold Setting (default 24h)
nodes.rationale: Low complexity; depends on detection. Thresholds become engine inputs rather than upload-time options.

nodes.label: Differentiator: Source-Level Breakdown (form vs email losses)
nodes.norm_label: differentiator: source-level breakdown (form vs email losses)
nodes.rationale: Med complexity; depends on normalization metadata being retained per source.

nodes.label: Table Stakes
nodes.rationale: Features without which the product is not credible in this category; all are Low or Med complexity.

nodes.label: Two Connection Cards (paste URL into form tool / forward emails here)
nodes.norm_label: two connection cards (paste url into form tool / forward emails here)
nodes.rationale: Exactly two options keeps the setup decision trivial for a non-technical owner.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Webhook Endpoint per Customer with Secret URL
nodes.norm_label: table stake: webhook endpoint per customer with secret url
nodes.rationale: Low complexity; depends on backend.

nodes.label: Differentiator: Weekly Digest Email ('you recovered/left $X')
nodes.rationale: Low complexity; depends on a digest job.

nodes.label: Settings Move from Client State to DB
nodes.norm_label: settings move from client state to db
nodes.rationale: Thresholds must live server-side because they drive detection running in cron and on ingest, not just in the client session.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant Postgres with RLS (packages/db)
nodes.rationale: Seven tables with RLS on all of them, isolation proven by test with a working negative control. Isolation is enforced in the database rather than the application so a handler bug cannot leak across tenants.

nodes.label: Isolation negative control (test:prove-isolation)
nodes.rationale: Loosening a single policy must turn the isolation suite red; this proves the suite is capable of failing and therefore that its green result means something.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Multi-tenant foundation (complete)
nodes.rationale: Delivered 7 tables with RLS enabled at creation time, 8 authenticated plus 6 ingest policies, 124 green tests across 9 files, and a JWT-to-customer resolver — deliberately with no UI, because tenant isolation had to be provable before anything was built on top of it.

nodes.label: Six-phase v2.0 milestone structure
nodes.rationale: v2.0 is decomposed into six phases tracked as 1 of 6 complete (17%), so an infrastructure-heavy milestone still reports discrete, verifiable increments rather than one long unbounded build.

nodes.label: Test command matrix (Docker requirements per suite)
nodes.norm_label: test command matrix (docker requirements per suite)
nodes.rationale: Suites are split by whether they need Docker so the fast, Docker-free core and web tests stay runnable everywhere while DB and API suites carry the container dependency.

nodes.label: Decision: ingest uses a NOBYPASSRLS role, not service_role
nodes.norm_label: decision: ingest uses a nobypassrls role, not service_role
nodes.rationale: Webhook ingest has no auth.uid(), so the obvious move is the service key — which bypasses RLS entirely. Instead a dedicated ingest_role reads a transaction-local app.customer_id, so a handler bug cannot write across tenants. Verified under test; the service-role fallback was never needed.

nodes.label: Lesson: a security test that cannot fail is worse than none
nodes.norm_label: lesson: a security test that cannot fail is worse than none
nodes.rationale: An isolation suite that passes unconditionally provides false assurance, so the negative control is run deliberately: loosen a policy and assert the suite goes red (npm run test:prove-isolation -w @missed-lead/db).

nodes.label: Lesson: RLS grants nothing
nodes.rationale: Policies filter only within privileges a role already holds. Drizzle emits CREATE POLICY but never GRANT, so the first migration left the authenticated role unable to read anything (error 42501). Nothing warns you — the isolation test caught it. Fixed in migration 0002_grants.sql.

nodes.label: Decision: Supabase for both auth and database
nodes.norm_label: decision: supabase for both auth and database
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Neon on 2026-08-24 despite the research doc recommending Neon. RLS policies need auth.uid(); with a single vendor the database reads the verified JWT natively, so tenant isolation genuinely lives in the DB rather than in application code. Neon's stateless HTTP driver additionally cannot hold the per-transaction setting the ingest role depends on.

nodes.norm_label: build step 6: dashboard upgrade + settings screens

nodes.norm_label: build step 3: email inbound worker into same pipeline

nodes.norm_label: build step 5: push notifications (mobile then pwa) + content

nodes.norm_label: pitfall 9: permission asked cold at first launch causes permanent denial
nodes.rationale: Prevention: ask after the first value moment (the first ingested lead) with a pre-permission explainer. Phase 5.

nodes.label: Push Notification Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering cold permission asks and token rot.

nodes.label: Pitfall 10: Push Token Rot
nodes.rationale: Uninstalled apps keep dead tokens and sends fail silently. Prevention: prune on expired/invalid responses and track last-seen. Phase 5.

nodes.label: Suggested Build Order (dependency-driven)
nodes.rationale: Ordering is derived from dependencies rather than perceived value: tenancy underpins everything, then each ingest pipe, then detection, then delivery, then reporting polish.

nodes.label: Deep Link to Lead Detail Screen
nodes.norm_label: deep link to lead detail screen
nodes.rationale: Both push channels converge on one deep link so a tap always lands on the actionable lead.

nodes.label: Notification Dispatcher (Expo push + web-push)
nodes.rationale: Single dispatcher with a per-device token registry so mobile and PWA delivery share one send path.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Push Notification with Dollar Amount + Deep Link
nodes.norm_label: table stake: push notification with dollar amount + deep link
nodes.rationale: Med complexity; depends on accounts and detection.

nodes.label: Expo Push Notifications (expo-notifications) (mobile push recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Native to the existing Expo 57 stack with a generous free tier.

nodes.label: FCM/APNs Direct Wiring (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: duplicates what Expo already abstracts.

nodes.label: OneSignal and similar push services (rejected for now)
nodes.norm_label: onesignal and similar push services (rejected for now)
nodes.rationale: Deferred until scale demands it; standard Web Push needs no vendor.

nodes.label: Versions to Verify at Plan-Phase (@neondatabase/serverless, drizzle-orm, expo-notifications, web-push, mailparser)
nodes.norm_label: versions to verify at plan-phase (@neondatabase/serverless, drizzle-orm, expo-notifications, web-push, mailparser)

nodes.norm_label: web push api via web-push library (web pwa push recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Standard API with no service dependency, and the PWA already uses workbox.

nodes.label: Context7 Version Verification Deferred to Plan-Phase
nodes.norm_label: context7 version verification deferred to plan-phase
nodes.rationale: Inline research could not confirm package versions, so verification is explicitly deferred rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Email Ingestion Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering mail loops, spam floods and encoding mangling; all land in the email-inbound phase.

nodes.label: Prevention: High-Entropy Secret in Hook URL Path
nodes.norm_label: prevention: high-entropy secret in hook url path
nodes.rationale: Unknown tokens are rejected silently and requests are rate-limited per IP, so scanners get no signal that a path exists.

nodes.label: Pitfall 6: HTML/Quoted-Printable Mangling Produces Garbage Contact Fields
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 6: html/quoted-printable mangling produces garbage contact fields
nodes.rationale: Prevention: let mailparser handle encodings, never regex raw bodies, use LLM extraction only for the free-text intent field with schema-validated output, and flag low-confidence results rather than guessing. Phase 3.

nodes.label: Prevention: Lightweight Spam Scoring + Visible Quarantine
nodes.norm_label: prevention: lightweight spam scoring + visible quarantine
nodes.rationale: Scoring runs before LLM extraction to save cost, and quarantine is visible in the UI so real leads are never lost silently.

nodes.label: Pitfall 4: Mail Loop
nodes.rationale: Our own notification email gets forwarded back into the inbound address. Prevention: skip messages whose from contains our domain, add an X-MissedLead header and drop echoes. Phase 3.

nodes.label: Prevention: Schema-Validated LLM Extraction, Flag Instead of Guess
nodes.norm_label: prevention: schema-validated llm extraction, flag instead of guess
nodes.rationale: LLM is confined to the free-text intent field with validated output; low confidence flags for review rather than fabricating a value.

nodes.label: Pitfall 5: Spam Floods Inbox and Junk Leads Pollute Revenue Estimates
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 5: spam floods inbox and junk leads pollute revenue estimates
nodes.rationale: Prevention: lightweight spam scoring before LLM extraction plus an auto-quarantine folder visible in the UI. Phase 3.

nodes.label: Prevention: X-MissedLead Header and Own-Domain Sender Skip
nodes.norm_label: prevention: x-missedlead header and own-domain sender skip
nodes.rationale: Two independent guards (header marker plus from-domain check) stop our own notifications re-entering the pipeline.

nodes.label: mailparser + LLM Extraction Step (email-body parsing recommendation)
nodes.norm_label: mailparser + llm extraction step (email-body parsing recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic header parsing via mailparser, with the LLM used only for free-text contact/intent fields.

nodes.label: Pure-LLM Extraction of Structured Headers (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: headers are deterministic, so an LLM adds cost and nondeterminism for no gain.

nodes.label: Accepted architecture consequences
nodes.rationale: Automatic capture forces a real backend for webhook receivers and token storage (serverless on Vercel is acceptable), a multi-tenant database with per-customer isolation, and push notifications on both Expo and PWA — the current static PWA plus Expo app cannot host integrations at all.

nodes.label: CSV upload retained as backfill
nodes.rationale: Kept rather than removed so customers can load history and so the product still works before any integration is connected.

nodes.label: Leak detection rules engine
nodes.rationale: Lives in packages/core and was built TDD-first so the rules deciding what counts as a leaked lead are verifiable independently of any UI or data source.

nodes.label: Normalized Lead schema (single convergence point)
nodes.rationale: Every ingestion source normalizes into one Lead schema that feeds the existing core engine, so adding a source never forks leak detection or revenue estimation.

nodes.label: Continuous detection with push notifications
nodes.rationale: Expo push on mobile plus PWA web push turn the product from something the owner must open into something that interrupts them with a dollar figure.

nodes.label: Revenue estimation engine
nodes.rationale: Converts detected leaks into a dollar figure — the single number the product sells — which is why dedupe correctness upstream is treated as a correctness-critical concern.

nodes.label: Decision: backend jump accepted for v2
nodes.norm_label: decision: backend jump accepted for v2
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant DB plus serverless API is accepted into v2 scope because integrations cannot be hosted by a static PWA. All sources normalize into the same Lead schema feeding the existing core engine, so the jump adds infrastructure without forking the detection logic.

nodes.label: Decision: ingest is read-only on detection_settings
nodes.norm_label: decision: ingest is read-only on detection_settings
nodes.rationale: An inbound webhook has no business changing a customer's configuration. Missing settings fall back to engine defaults instead of erroring, so detection is never blocked by absent config.

nodes.label: Lesson: the parser silently disabled three of four leak rules
nodes.norm_label: lesson: the parser silently disabled three of four leak rules
nodes.rationale: last_contact_at and next_follow_up_at were header-mapped but never written, so every CSV lead looked unanswered and only one rule effectively ran. Re-check this whenever the Lead shape changes.

nodes.label: packages/ui (Tamagui design system)
nodes.rationale: One Tamagui component library shared by the Vite PWA and the Expo app so web and mobile do not diverge visually or in behavior.

nodes.label: Deliberately broad target customer
nodes.rationale: Local service businesses, CRM-using agencies/coaches and website owners are all in scope with no exclusive wedge segment: integration order substitutes for segmentation, so whichever source ships first implicitly selects the early customers.

nodes.label: Problem: manual CSV export friction
nodes.rationale: Around 90% of target customers are non-technical local business owners who will never gather or export lead data manually, so the product must observe leads automatically, report missed revenue proactively, and then recover those leads.

nodes.label: Personal WhatsApp is blocked (no official API)
nodes.norm_label: personal whatsapp is blocked (no official api)
nodes.rationale: No official API exists; coverage is only possible through a Business Platform migration, so personal WhatsApp is excluded rather than half-supported.

nodes.label: Source access reality matrix
nodes.rationale: Researched 2026-08-23: CRMs expose open OAuth APIs (low friction), forms/Calendly/Typeform expose webhooks (trivial), Gmail/Outlook are gated by Google verification (weeks), IG/FB DMs need professional accounts plus Meta App Review (hard), and personal WhatsApp has no official API at all (blocked). This friction ranking, not customer preference, sets the build order.

nodes.label: Core Value Priority
nodes.rationale: Ordered deliberately: (1) show lost revenue in money terms is the hook that makes the product legible to a non-technical owner, (2) zero-effort capture is the moat and the v2 focus, (3) automatic recovery is the expansion. Value must be proven in dollars before asking for data access or autonomy.

nodes.label: Phase/milestone document evolution process
nodes.rationale: PROJECT.md is revised only at phase transitions and milestone boundaries via /gsd-transition and /gsd-complete-milestone, so scope, validated capabilities and decisions are re-audited on a fixed cadence instead of drifting continuously.

nodes.label: Decision Record — Automated Lead Capture & Recovery
nodes.norm_label: decision record — automated lead capture & recovery
nodes.rationale: Exploration session following the v1 CSV-upload release, recording decisions on sources, access strategy, scope and autonomy posture (dated 2026-08-23).

nodes.label: Zero-effort data capture (the moat)
nodes.rationale: Manual CSV upload puts the work on the customer, and roughly 90% of target customers will never gather or export lead data by hand. Automatic ingestion is therefore not a convenience feature but the defensible core of v2.

nodes.label: Email-forwarding ingestion (@in.missedlead.app inbox)
nodes.rationale: A unique inbound inbox via Cloudflare Email Routing or Postmark captures leads from tools that only send email notifications, again without any OAuth verification process.

nodes.label: Gmail read-only OAuth
nodes.rationale: Treated as a convenience upgrade rather than a foundation because Google verification takes weeks and would block launch if depended on.

nodes.label: Integration order (four phases)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 webhooks plus email forwarding, Phase 2 CRM OAuth, Phase 3 Gmail read-only OAuth as a convenience upgrade, Phase 4 the Meta stack. Ordering by approval friction means shipping value before depending on any third-party reviewer.

nodes.label: Meta stack (Instagram/Facebook DMs)
nodes.rationale: Last in order: only professional accounts are readable and Meta App Review gates access, so effort here is high-risk relative to the leads it unlocks.

nodes.label: Webhook ingestion (unique URL per customer)
nodes.rationale: Works day one with zero platform approvals: the customer pastes a URL into an existing form or scheduling tool, which is the lowest-friction path to automatic capture.

nodes.label: Milestone v2.0 — Automated Lead Capture & Recovery
nodes.norm_label: milestone v2.0 — automated lead capture & recovery
nodes.rationale: Replaces manual CSV upload with automatic ingestion plus proactive missed-revenue alerts, and accepts a backend and multi-tenant persistence as the cost of doing so.

nodes.label: Non-technical onboarding flows
nodes.rationale: Onboarding is reduced to pasting a webhook URL or adding an email filter, because any step requiring developer skills reintroduces the friction zero-effort capture exists to remove.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Webhook ingest (next)
nodes.rationale: Framed as the first user-visible value. Because the repository functions it needs already exist and are tested, Phase 2 reduces to the HTTP endpoint, token issuance and rotation, rate limiting, and the 'we're listening' test-connection UX.

nodes.label: Ingestion source order (webhooks and email first)
nodes.norm_label: ingestion source order (webhooks and email first)
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-08-23: webhooks plus email forwarding first because they need zero platform approvals and work day one; CRM OAuth second; Gmail OAuth third; Meta last because App Review and Google verification add weeks of gated risk before any customer value.

nodes.label: Draft-and-approve follow-ups (one-tap send)
nodes.rationale: The middle rung of the autonomy ladder: the system writes the message and the owner sends it with one tap, which both saves time and generates the approve/edit telemetry that later justifies full autonomy.

nodes.label: Explicitly deferred scope
nodes.rationale: CRM OAuth connectors, Gmail read-only OAuth, the Meta stack (IG/FB/WhatsApp) and automated follow-up/booking are all deferred: the integrations because they require platform approvals that gate delivery, and the automation because autonomy is graduated and must be earned per the full-auto-booking seed.

nodes.label: Approval-rate telemetry as autonomy gate
nodes.rationale: Approve-without-edit rate is the measurable proxy for whether drafts are trustworthy in a category, turning an otherwise subjective trust decision into a threshold.

nodes.label: Full-auto booking behavior
nodes.rationale: Auto-reply within minutes of a new inquiry, propose slots from the connected calendar, confirm the booking, and send the owner a daily activity digest — speed is the value, and the digest preserves owner oversight without requiring per-message attention.

nodes.label: Always-on autonomy guardrails
nodes.rationale: Even in full-auto mode the system escalates pricing commitments, refunds/discounts, negative sentiment and low-confidence cases to a human, respects owner-defined quiet hours by queueing until morning, caps autonomous touches per lead (e.g. 2), and keeps per-category switches plus a global kill switch — the classes of mistake that would destroy trust are structurally removed from the model's reach.

nodes.label: Full-auto unlock criteria
nodes.rationale: At least 20-30 drafts sent in a category with 90%+ approved without edits, and even then offered only as an explicit opt-in toggle ('Auto-answer new inquiries?') per category and per customer — so autonomy is never switched on without both evidence and consent.

nodes.label: Seed: Full-Auto Booking Engine
nodes.rationale: Planted 2026-08-23 as the graduated-autonomy end-state; triggered only after draft-and-approve ships and a lead category reaches ~90% approve-without-edit over 20-30 drafts for a given customer.

nodes.label: Autonomy posture rationale (graduated)
nodes.rationale: Full-auto on day one destroys trust on the first mistake; approve-only forever fails busy owners and defeats the product promise. The graduated ladder — detect and notify, then draft and approve, then per-customer per-category full-auto after ~90% approve-without-edit over 20-30 drafts, always with escalation rules, quiet hours and toggles — earns autonomy from measured telemetry.

nodes.label: Graduated autonomy posture
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-08-23. v2 detects and notifies only; draft-and-approve follow-ups come next; full-auto unlocks later per approval-rate telemetry. Full autonomy on day one destroys trust on the first mistake, while approve-forever fails busy owners and defeats the product promise — so autonomy is earned from telemetry rather than granted.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Email Worker (Gmail filter forward receiver)
nodes.norm_label: cloudflare email worker (gmail filter forward receiver)
nodes.rationale: Gmail forwarding hits an Email Worker that POSTs into the same ingest API, avoiding a second pipeline.

nodes.label: Ingest API (/api/hook/[token].ts, /api/inbound-email.ts)
nodes.rationale: Single entry point that validates, normalizes, dedupes, persists and triggers detection per customer, so every source shares one funnel.

nodes.label: Building SMTP Ourselves (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: enormous undifferentiated effort versus a hosted routing hop.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Email Routing to Email Worker to Ingestion API (inbound email recommendation)
nodes.norm_label: cloudflare email routing to email worker to ingestion api (inbound email recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Free, programmable, and has no approval queue, unlike commercial inbound-email services.

nodes.label: Express Server on a VM (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: adds infrastructure to operate when Vercel functions already suffice for stateless receivers.

nodes.label: Hono / Nitro Meta-Frameworks (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: Vercel functions suffice, so an extra server framework is unearned complexity.

nodes.label: IMAP Polling (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: polling adds latency and statefulness where push-style routing is available.

nodes.label: Postmark Inbound (~$15/mo alternative)
nodes.rationale: Named fallback if Cloudflare Email Routing proves insufficient; costs roughly $15/mo.

nodes.label: Vercel Serverless/Edge Functions (backend runtime recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Zero new infra since web already deploys to Vercel; webhook and inbound-email receivers are small stateless functions.

nodes.label: DB Layer (Drizzle schema: customers, lead_sources, leads, lead_events, detection_settings, push_tokens)
nodes.norm_label: db layer (drizzle schema: customers, lead_sources, leads, lead_events, detection_settings, push_tokens)
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant via customer_id FK on every row plus Postgres RLS so isolation is enforced at the database rather than in application code.

nodes.label: Compliance-Lite Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering unbounded PII retention; treated as a pre-launch checklist rather than early work.

nodes.label: Prevention: Retention Policy Field, Delete-Account Cascade, Privacy Policy
nodes.norm_label: prevention: retention policy field, delete-account cascade, privacy policy
nodes.rationale: Bounds PII exposure (e.g. purge after 12 months) and is gated as a pre-public-launch requirement.

nodes.label: Prevention: RLS on All Tables at Migration Time + Cross-Tenant Test
nodes.norm_label: prevention: rls on all tables at migration time + cross-tenant test
nodes.rationale: Enabling RLS during migration makes it the default state, and the integration test turns tenant isolation into a regression-checked property.

nodes.label: Pitfall 13: End-Customer PII Stored Without Bounds
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 13: end-customer pii stored without bounds
nodes.rationale: Prevention: a retention policy field (e.g. purge lead PII after 12 months), delete-account cascade, and a privacy policy page before public launch. Phase 6 pre-launch checklist.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM (ORM/query recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Tiny, edge-compatible and SQL-shaped, matching the TypeScript monorepo.

nodes.label: Prisma ORM (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected for engine weight on Edge runtimes.

nodes.label: Raw SQL Everywhere (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected as an unmaintainable extreme versus a thin SQL-shaped ORM.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Dashboard/Settings/Onboarding Polish + Retention & Compliance Checklist
nodes.norm_label: phase 6: dashboard/settings/onboarding polish + retention & compliance checklist

nodes.label: CSV Upload Path as Historical Backfill
nodes.norm_label: csv upload path as historical backfill
nodes.rationale: CSV path persists unchanged but writes to the same leads table, flagged source:'csv', so history and stream never diverge.

nodes.label: Normalized Lead Schema
nodes.rationale: All ingest paths normalize into the same Lead schema the CSV parser already emits, so the detection engine needs no rewrite.

nodes.label: Pitfall 12: CSV-Era Data vs Streamed Data Drift
nodes.norm_label: pitfall 12: csv-era data vs streamed data drift
nodes.rationale: Different null semantics and timestamps between the two paths. Prevention: one table from day one, with CSV backfill writing through the same normalizer. Phase 2.

nodes.label: Data Correctness Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Category covering double-counted revenue and CSV-vs-stream drift; both are ultimately schema-design problems.

nodes.label: Prevention: One Leads Table with a Shared Normalizer
nodes.norm_label: prevention: one leads table with a shared normalizer
nodes.rationale: CSV backfill writes through the same normalizer as the stream, so null semantics and timestamps cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: packages/core ingest/normalize Adapters
nodes.rationale: Adapters export the SAME Lead schema the CSV parser emits so the engine stays untouched.

nodes.label: Detection Input Shifts from File-at-Rest to Event Stream
nodes.norm_label: detection input shifts from file-at-rest to event stream
nodes.rationale: The engine becomes a library called by ingest and cron rather than an upload handler; this is the central data-flow change of v2.

nodes.label: One Funnel, Many Pipes
nodes.rationale: The architectural shape in a phrase: every source normalizes into the Lead schema that already feeds packages/core, so adding a channel never forks the pipeline.

nodes.label: Auth (email OAuth sign-in + session to customer_id middleware)
nodes.norm_label: auth (email oauth sign-in + session to customer_id middleware)
nodes.rationale: Email OAuth avoids passwords for non-technical owners; middleware resolves session to customer_id so tenancy is applied uniformly.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenancy via customer_id
nodes.rationale: customer_id FK on every row is the single tenancy primitive, enforced by RLS instead of query-time filtering.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres with RLS by customer_id
nodes.norm_label: neon postgres with rls by customer_id
nodes.rationale: Stores leads, events, customers, push_tokens and settings with row-level security keyed on customer_id.

nodes.label: Table Stake: Multi-Tenant Account with Email OAuth Login
nodes.norm_label: table stake: multi-tenant account with email oauth login
nodes.rationale: Low complexity; depends on DB.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled JWT Sessions (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: security-critical plumbing better delegated to a managed auth provider.

nodes.label: Postgres RLS Tenant Isolation (rows scoped by customer_id)
nodes.norm_label: postgres rls tenant isolation (rows scoped by customer_id)
nodes.rationale: RLS means tenant isolation is enforced at the database, not in application code, so a forgotten WHERE clause cannot leak data.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth or Clerk (auth/multi-tenant recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Provides OAuth email sign-in suited to non-technical owners without hand-rolling sessions.

nodes.label: Ingest repository functions (upsertLead, recordLeadEvent, buildDedupeKey, withIngestScope)
nodes.norm_label: ingest repository functions (upsertlead, recordleadevent, builddedupekey, withingestscope)

nodes.label: Decision: contact splits into email/phone in the DB
nodes.norm_label: decision: contact splits into email/phone in the db
nodes.rationale: The in-memory Lead type keeps one polymorphic contact field and hydration sets contact = email ?? phone. A single unvalidated column cannot be deduped, and dedupe is what prevents the same person being counted twice — which would corrupt the one number the product sells.

nodes.label: Decision: merge policy is a pure function (mergeLeadFields)
nodes.norm_label: decision: merge policy is a pure function (mergeleadfields)
nodes.rationale: Keeping the merge rules as a pure function makes the logic deciding whether a second sighting of a lead improves or corrupts the record testable without a database.

nodes.label: Decision: two dedupe mechanisms, not one
nodes.norm_label: decision: two dedupe mechanisms, not one
nodes.rationale: lead_events.dedupe_key handles retried deliveries; lead_identities handles the same human arriving through different channels. One key cannot do both jobs, and a single lead may hold several contact points.

nodes.label: v1 limitations
nodes.rationale: No integrations, no sending, no auth or billing, no AI scoring, browser-local processing and no backend — each exclusion keeps v1 shippable as a proof of the revenue hook alone.
